curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: realise the role of vocabulary in language acquisition.

interactions.prompt: A learner discovers that 'enormous' means very big. What has grown?
interactions.feedback: Yes! Learning a new word grows vocabulary.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the collection of words a person knows.

interactions.prompt: Why is learning the word 'seedling' useful?
choices: It helps us name and talk about a young plant.
interactions.answer: It helps us name and talk about a young plant.
interactions.feedback: Correct! Vocabulary gives us precise names and ideas.
interactions.retryHint: Words help us describe and communicate.

interactions.prompt: Match each new word to what it helps us express.
interactions.feedback: Word power! Each new word adds meaning.
interactions.retryHint: Use the meaning clue beside each word.

interactions.prompt: Toma knows 'hot' but learns 'warm' and 'boiling'. How does this help him?
choices: He can describe temperatures more exactly.
interactions.answer: He can describe temperatures more exactly.
interactions.feedback: Exactly! More vocabulary makes messages clearer.
interactions.retryHint: Compare how specific the three temperature words are.

interactions.prompt: Amina meets the word 'fragile' on a parcel and learns it means easily broken. What can she now do?
choices: Understand the warning and handle it carefully.
interactions.answer: Understand the warning and handle it carefully.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! New vocabulary supports understanding and action.
interactions.retryHint: Use the new meaning to protect the parcel.

interactions.prompt: Which statement best explains the role of vocabulary in learning language?
choices: New words help us understand, speak, read and write more clearly.
One word is enough for every idea.
Vocabulary matters only during spelling tests.
interactions.answer: New words help us understand, speak, read and write more clearly.
interactions.feedback: Word-power champion! You understand why vocabulary matters.
interactions.retryHint: Choose the answer covering all ways we use language.
